Agents log counterparties per task; afterward, graph clustering flags tight groups whose internal interaction share exceeds a threshold, and those accounts face delayed settlement. To evade, an attacker must sustain costly diverse external activity against a gale of organic traffic, making each fake identity pay real fees and latency. Honest agents harbor no penalty since their edges spread widely, while sybil rings stay trapped in a closed lagoon of self-dealing.
